haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is created or sent.
haiku-low.q2: No row is created and no email is sent. They see the same generic message as every request case.
haiku-low.q3: It works for 30 minutes from issue. A newer link issued for the account burns it, and saving the password uses it up.
haiku-low.q4: Nothing changes. The link stays unused and usable until expiry, so the user can retry the password.
haiku-low.q5: No devices stay logged in; all sessions for the account are deleted, including the one that did the reset. The user logs in again with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token goes into the mail job; the worker builds the link from it and sends it. Only the hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the URL token and looks up the reset_tokens row by the indexed hash. It checks the row is present, unexpired and unused.
haiku-low.q9: In the reset_tokens table: a count of the account's rows created in the rolling hour. Rows are never deleted, so old ones fall out of the window.
haiku-low.q10: At issue time, inside the request transaction before commit, the account's unused reset_tokens rows get used time set. They are not deleted.
haiku-low.q11: Burning the token, updating the password hash and deleting all sessions commit together. The password-changed email job is queued in that same transaction before commit.
haiku-low.q12: A conditional update sets used time only if the row is still unused and unexpired. The second submit updates nothing, rolls back and sees the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic message ("If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link."). Nothing is created or sent.
sonnet.q2: Nothing: the transaction ends with no change, no row is created, no email is sent, and they still see the generic message (limit is 3 per account per rolling hour).
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from issue (expiry = issue time + 30 min). It ends sooner if used (password saved) or if a newer link is requested for the account, which sets used time on the older unused rows.
sonnet.q4: Unchanged and still usable until it expires. The token is not changed; the reason is shown on the form and the user can try again.
sonnet.q5: None. All sessions rows for the account are deleted, including the device that did the reset. The user is redirected to the login page, not logged in, and logs in again with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told; they can request again, which counts against the limit.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is placed in the "reset link" job on the Email queue. The Email worker builds the link from the raw token and sends it through the Mail provider. The job holds the raw token until sent or dropped.
sonnet.q8: It hashes the token from the URL and looks up the reset_tokens row by that hash (the hash column is indexed). If the row is missing, expired, or has used time set, it shows the expired page; otherwise the link is valid.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED as a separate counter. The count is taken from reset_tokens rows for the account created in the rolling hour (rows are never deleted). Old requests drop out because the count only includes the last 60 minutes.
sonnet.q10: During the request (A), after the rate-limit check passes and within the transaction, used time is set on the account's unused reset_tokens rows (burned, not deleted). Then the new row is inserted and the job queued, before commit.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: burning the link (setting used time), updating the users password hash, deleting all the account's sessions rows, and adding the "password changed" job to the Email queue. The confirmation job is queued as part of that same transaction, before commit (atomic only if the queue is in Postgres, which is an open question).
sonnet.q12: A conditional update in the transaction sets used time only if the row is still unused and unexpired. Only one succeeds; the other updates no row, rolls back, and sees the expired page.
